responsibilities: Become a founding member of Saily's Data team and take the lead in building the entire vertical yourself.
Own data modeling and schema design across Saily.
Take raw, unmodelled data and turn it into clean, scalable data models.
Build a clear semantic layer with consistent entities, relationships, metrics, and definitions.
Make our data easy to understand and use - both for people and AI.
Own and evolve our analytics infrastructure and tooling.
Set standards around data quality, documentation, naming, and governance.
Work closely with Product, Engineering, Marketing and other teams to understand their data needs and make sure our models reflect how Saily actually works.
Help shape how Data Analytics operates as Saily grows.

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Set standards around data quality, documentation, naming, and governance.
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Quality, documentation, naming and governance standards are an explicit responsibility; "Saily is growing fast" is the only speed phrase and it describes the company, not the work.
evidence.domain_risk: Saily has millions of paying customers and hundreds of thousands of travelers browsing through Saily at any given moment.
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: Consumer eSIM analytics at scale, but the models serve internal analysis with no financial-reporting or regulatory language.
evidence.collaboration_width: Product; Engineering; Marketing; Data Analytics team
evidence.data_team_maturity: Become a founding member of Saily's Data team and take the lead in building the entire vertical yourself.
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: Founding member of a Data team that does not yet exist, building the vertical from raw unmodelled data.
evidence.jd_authorship: Build a clear semantic layer with consistent entities, relationships, metrics, and definitions.
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: The bullets name the modelling artefacts precisely and the stack is listed down to Clickhouse and coding agents.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: we need to turn it into clear, reliable models that humans (i.e. Data Analytics team) and AI can actually understand and use
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The posting names the Data Analytics team as the consumer of the semantic layer this role builds.
evidence.autonomy_level: take the lead in building the entire vertical yourself
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: The role owns modelling, architecture, standards and how Data Analytics operates as the company grows.
evidence.ai_role: Make our data easy to understand and use - both for people and AI.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: The candidate models the data so AI systems can consume it, and coding agents also appear in the stack — the enabler signal is the stronger one.
evidence.testing_framing: Set standards around data quality, documentation, naming, and governance.
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: The candidate sets the data quality standards for the whole vertical, rather than being asked to know a testing tool.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: The posting is written entirely as capability-building for a founding hire, with no incidents, compliance or cost-of-error framing.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: Take raw, unmodelled data and turn it into clean, scalable data models.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: The data is explicitly unmodelled and the team does not yet exist — everything is built from scratch.
evidence.work_arrangement: Work from anywhere: work from wherever keeps you in the zone.
